state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The negative-sloping section on a distance-time graph does not mean Fido has fallen asleep. It actually represents Fido moving away from his home. Remember to consider the direction of the graph when interpreting the movement.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, okay! So the negative slope means Fido is moving away from home instead of sleeping. But how do I know when he’s moving towards home again? Is it just when the line goes back up?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The negative slope on a distance-time graph does indicate that Fido is moving away from home, not sleeping. To determine when Fido is moving towards home again, you need to look for when the graph starts sloping back up towards the x-axis. Remember to consider the direction of the line to interpret the movement correctly.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher makes a critical mathematical error by stating that negative slope means moving away from home (when it actually means moving toward home/decreasing distance), simply tells the answer without engaging the student's reasoning about rest vs. movement, and the student's Turn 2 response shows confusion rather than understanding.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides some direct corrective feedback but makes a significant conceptual error (stating negative slope means moving away when it actually means moving toward home), lacks explicit procedural steps for graph interpretation, and doesn't demonstrate worked examples characteristic of rule-based instruction.
